dedupe_keys.name: telecommunications damage restoration and countermeasures after the great east japan earthquake 2011

description: This recovery and redesign case documents what the earthquake and tsunami of 11 March 2011 did to Japan's telecommunications and what was changed afterwards. According to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, about 1.2 million fixed lines and about 15,000 mobile base stations became unusable (up to about 29,000 across five mobile operators), more than 80 per cent because of long, wide-area commercial power cuts that exhausted batteries, while the tsunami destroyed exchange buildings and cables; NTT alone reported about 1,000 exchange offices affected and mobilised some 6,000 staff for restoration. Operators restored most service by the end of April 2011 with mobile and small base stations and by converting mountaintop sites into large-zone stations that each cover the areas of several ordinary ones. A ministry study group on securing communications in large-scale emergencies issued a final report in November 2011, leading to large-zone base stations in major cities, longer battery and generator back-up, route diversity and congestion measures, and the events are reported in the 2011 white paper on information and communications. Coverage: north-eastern Japan (mainly Iwate, Miyagi and Fukushima), 2011, with countermeasures nationwide. Format and access: free Japanese-language white paper, study-group report and briefing papers; NTT press releases in English. Caveats: statistics are operator-reported; much detail is only in Japanese. Simulation uses: fragility of telecom sites to power loss, earthquake and tsunami, restoration curves for fixed and mobile networks, and design of power back-up and large-zone coverage. Related records: the FCC Katrina panel and Tonga cable cut cases are other disaster recoveries.
